The '''Forsaken''' is an enemy in Monster Train 2. It is a weak early-game enemy that can appear in the [[Trials#Mark_of_Invasion|Mark of Invasion]] trial in Rings 1 and 2.

== Strategy ==
The '''Forsaken''' are the weakest enemies in the game, but they often enter in large numbers, especially when summoned by a Trial. {{IconLink|Sweep}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike}} are more effective than high {{Attack}}, and weak but spammable spells like [[Witchweave]] or [[Glimmer]] can take them out easily. They will instantly die upon attacking a unit with {{IconLink|Spikes}}, which makes them ideal for triggering {{IconLink|Slay}} on [[Little Fade]]'s '''Little Icarus''' path.

An artifact like [[Jackstrips]] or [[Rules of Containment]] will kill '''Forsaken''' after combat ends on the bottom floor.

The '''Cowering Sycophant''' is an enemy in Monster Train 2. It does not attack, but starts with high {{IconLink|Armor}} and {{IconLink|Spikes}} which damage your units when attacked.

== Strategy ==
Avoid letting your fragile backliners attack these enemies. If possible, kill them with spells to avoid damage to your units. Due to their {{IconLink|Armor}}, [[piercing]] spells like [[Horn Break]] are effective.

Units with high base {{Attack}} are better than those which depend on {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, as they will only be damaged by {{IconLink|Spikes}} once.

If using [[Hornbreaker Prince]]'s '''Reaper''' path, be aware that the [[Heavenly Toll]] combat features three '''Cowering Sycophants''' at Covenant 2 and above. If he attacks all three of them, their combined {{IconLink|Spikes}} will deal exactly enough damage to kill him, and he will not be able to contribute to the boss fight. Have a plan in mind to either eliminate them before he can attack, protect him with {{IconLink|Armor}} or other effects, or remove them from his path (perhaps via '''[[Ascend]]''' cards like [[Hidden Passage]]).

The '''Sloven Knight''' is an enemy in Monster Train 2. It is weak, but has high {{Health}} and gains {{Attack|+8}} if no other enemies are in front of it.

== Strategy ==
In theory, their {{IconLink|Vanguard}} trigger means that it can be worth keeping other enemies in front of them alive to limit their damage output. However, in [[Heaven's Gate#Knights of Entropy|Knights of Entropy]] they appear behind a [[Savage Spearman]], which has {{Attack|6}}. This means that killing the Spearman only increases the total damage dealt by the enemy wave by 2, and allows your units to damage the '''Sloven Knight'''. In general, '''Sloven Knights''' should simply be treated like any other early game enemy with a large health pool: hit them until they die. However, it is much more dangerous to allow them to reach the Pyre than similar enemies like [[Fallen Champion]], as they will output a huge amount of damage.

The '''Lurking Miscreant''' is an enemy in Monster Train 2. It is a backline enemy in Rings 1-3 that pollutes your draw with [[Chime of Despair]].

== Strategy ==
Chime of Despair poses no threat to your Pyre, but does prevent you from drawing through your deck. The combats in Rings 1 and 2 are relatively short, and if you are relying on a key card to defeat the boss, you may not draw it in time if your draws are polluted with [[Scourge]]s. In this situation, it is best to kill '''Lurking Miscreants''' as quickly as possible. If multiple are present, kill those on the lower floors first, as they will have more turns in which to add Chimes to your deck. Weak spells like [[Torch]] and [[Witchweave]] are ideal for this.

If your units are strong enough to defeat the boss with minimal support from your deck, '''Lurking Miscreants''' can often be safely ignored. Unlike later Scourge enemies, the cards they add to your deck do not damage your Pyre.

The '''Energizing Flautist''' is an enemy in Monster Train 2. It grants allied enemies {{IconLink|Haste}}, causing them to move from the bottom floor directly to the top floor.

== Strategy ==
'''Energizing Flautists''' allow all enemies in the same wave to instantly move from the first floor to the third. This is potentially dangerous, as it gives you less time to prepare the top floor and prevents you from building defenses on the middle floor.

Ironically, '''Energizing Flautists''' may sometimes be more dangerous when dead. If you cannot consistently kill them every turn, it is often better to leave all of them alive: killing an '''Energizing Flautist''' on one wave but not the next means that both waves will reach the third floor at the same time, making them much harder to kill.

The Flautist can be especially dangerous with the Mark of Invasion [[Trial]], as the 5 [[Forsaken]] on the second floor will arrive on the top floor at the same time as the first wave of enemies. If none of these enemies have been killed beforehand, then a [[Savage Spearman]], along with the Flautist, will be pushed directly to the Pyre Room. A [[Shield Steward]] on the second floor is enough to kill one of the Forsaken and prevent this, but you will still need a way to kill four Forsaken, two Savage Spearmen, and a [[Fallen Champion]] in one turn.

{{IconLink|Haste}} has no effect on enemies which are already on the second floor. So if you have a way to {{IconLink|Mute}} or {{IconLink|Silence}} '''Energizing Flautists''' on the first floor, such as [[Zone of Silence]] or [[Unnamed Tome]], then they become completely harmless and are essentially a free {{IconLink|Slay}} or {{IconLink|Harvest}} trigger. Alternatively, '''[[Ascend]]ing''' them to the middle floor completely nullifies them.

In the '''[[High Heaven#Inevitability|Inevitability]]''' variant of [[Stryx]] & [[Hallow]], '''Energizing Flautists''' will spawn frequently and grant {{IconLink|Haste}} to Stryx, as well as other enemies that spawn during the waves. If left unchecked, this will grant her extra {{IconLink|Loop}} triggers and raise Hallow's {{Attack}} significantly.

'''Yorael the First-Blessed''' is one of the possible [[Ring 1]] Bosses. He is a simple, no-frills boss with high immediate damage output.

== Strategy ==
'''Yorael''' is a very different fight from [[Astreal the Lost]], the other Ring 1 boss. While Astreal's {{IconLink|Sap}} allows his damage to scale up during battle, '''Yorael''''s damage output can only decrease.

'''Yorael''' gains a stack of {{IconLink|Rage}} on {{IconLink|Slay}}, but loses a stack of {{IconLink|Rage}} each time he attacks. This means that his starting damage of {{Attack|14}} decreases by 2 each time he attacks but fails to kill the target, down to a minimum of {{Attack|8}}. Outside of your [[Champion]] and banner unit, the only starting unit which can survive a hit from him is a [[Shield Steward]]. You can take advantage of this by keeping your Shield Stewards in your deck until later in the battle, so that they will be at full or nearly full {{Health}} when Yorael arrives. He will lose {{Attack|2}} while fighting a Steward with at least {{Health|15}}, and once he has done so he will lose {{Attack|4}} against the next Steward as long as it has at least {{Health|23}}, or {{Attack|2}} if it has anywhere from {{Health|13}} to {{Health|22}}. If both Stewards have {{Health|14}} or less, he will remain at {{Attack|14}}.

This means that, by playing your Champion and banner unit on the top floor and waiting to play Stewards on the lower floors, you can decrease his damage from {{Attack|14}} to {{Attack|8}} by the time he reaches the top floor, resulting in a much easier fight for your Champion and banner unit. Starting with cards like [[Restore]] or [[Fortified Pauldrons]] can allow you to keep your Stewards at high enough {{Health}} to do this while still playing the Stewards during the Deployment phase.

Alternatively, you can simply not play any units on the lower floors, or allow them to be killed before Yorael arrives. If he ends battle on a floor without killing a unit, he will lose {{IconLink|Rage|1}}. If both lower floors are empty, he will reach the top floor with {{Attack|10}}.

Note that this may make it harder to deal with the earlier waves of enemies. Not only will you be unable to wear them down with the Shield Stewards' attacks, but you will also need to spend {{Ember}} and card draw to play the Stewards later on. This may cause you to leak enemies to the Pyre, but can be necessary to defeat '''Yorael''' if you started with a bad deck.

If the battle is [[Ring 1#Dominion's Preservation|Dominion's Preservation]], killing the [[Ominous Acolyte]] that spawns alongside him, either with first-floor {{IconLink|Sweep}} or damage spells, can help take him down faster. Spells are also good against [[Forsaken]] in [[Ring 1#Forsaken Few|Forsaken Few]], which will otherwise block the first few hits to '''Yorael''' and soften up your units for him.

'''Astreal the Lost''' is one of the possible [[Ring 1]] Bosses. He cannot attack at first due to his {{IconLink|Sap|6}}, but as combat is dragged out he will quickly become deadly.

== Strategy ==
'''Astreal''' can be dangerous for an unprepared player, but with the proper preparations he is one of the easiest bosses to defeat. A common early-game strategy is to place [[:Category:Steward units|Stewards]] and other disposable units on the lower floors to deal a small amount of damage to enemies, then put the Champion and other stronger units on the top floor to finish them off. Do ''not'' do this when facing '''Astreal'''.

While fighting your Stewards on the lower floors, '''Astreal''''s {{IconLink|Sap}} will wear off, massively increasing his damage by the time he reaches your main floor. He also heals on {{IconLink|Resolve}} at higher covenants, cancelling out most of the damage the Stewards have dealt to him. He will then easily tear your units apart before they can kill him. Instead, either build your main floor at the bottom and use Stewards higher up to mop up any survivors, or simply don't play Stewards at all. If '''Astreal''' arrives on a kill floor with all of his stacks of {{IconLink|Sap}} intact, he will be a sitting duck, easily killed before he can do any significant damage.

If you happen to get [[Unstable Pyresparks]] at the beginning of the game, it can usually trivialize '''Astreal''', allowing your Stewards to deal with enemy waves, then explode to deal 200 damage to '''Astreal''' and avoid reducing his {{IconLink|Sap}}.

== Strategy ==
Both Ring 2 bosses function as deck checks. While [[Legion]] tests your defensive abilities, particularly on backliners, '''Elebor''' tests your damage output. His attacks are weak, but he gains {{IconLink|Armor|5}} every turn, making builds which cannot put out reasonable damage every turn counterproductive. Quickly killing any other enemies which spawn alongside him, especially [[Savage Spearman]], will significantly reduce his damage output and give you more time to kill him.

Due to having {{IconLink|Titanskin|2}} and gaining {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} on {{IconLink|Resolve}} at Covenant 4 and above, '''Elebor''' is difficult to kill with spells. ===Strategy===
If you see that you're going to be fighting '''Furious Frenzy Arkion''', pick up cheap damaging spells like [[Flash Freeze]] or [[Inhale]] from early card rewards. The main goal here is to avoid killing his units in front of him, and so being able to control when they die is the most important part of the fight. Unlike your units, which will always attack the enemies on their same floor, spells can be used on any floor, allowing you to pick off enemies like [[Savage Spearman]] easily while '''Arkion''' is elsewhere.

Otherwise, it can be good to build a kill floor on the bottom floor, and fill the top floors with cheap but tanky units such as [[Shield Steward]]. This means that '''Arkion''' will spend much of the battle on higher floors, while all of the other enemies die before reaching those floors. However, this requires already having a strategy strong enough to consistently kill all enemies within a single floor.

It is usually best to avoid playing units on all three floors if your kill floor is at the top, as Arkion will not travel to empty floors. If Arkion goes from floor 1, to floor 2, to floor 3 in that order, then you will have no way to kill the units in that wave without giving him an enormous amount of Rage. It is often a good idea to leave the middle floor empty, even if you have units which can be played there, so that you can safely kill enemies with spells as they pass through that floor.

Spells that can '''[[Ascend]]''' and '''[[Descend]]''', like [[Hidden Passage]] and [[Gravity]], are extremely useful in this fight for moving '''Arkion''' away from units that are about to die.

If not properly controlled, '''Arkion''' will often have {{Attack|30}} or more going into {{IconLink|Relentless}}, making it easy for him to smash his way through your units before they can take him down.

Note that Arkion moves ''after'' other enemies. This means that if you have [[Jackstrips]], enemies like Savage Spearman can move onto the floor where Arkion was on the previous turn, die to the damage from Jackstrips, and buff his Rage before he moves to another floor.

'''Hard Headed''' can either be completely irrelevant, or one of the most difficult boss modifiers in the game. For clans like [[Banished]] with easy access to movement options, it's simple to move your tanks back to the front once he's shoved them to the back, and can even be beneficial as it will trigger {{IconLink|Shift}} on the entire floor, but many clans do not have any '''[[Advance]]''' or '''[[Retreat]]''' cards. A more consistent strategy is to avoid builds which rely on a tanky frontliner to protect a fragile backliner.

Keep in mind that if '''Arkion''' attacks the same floor multiple times, he can push your units back to their original position in time for {{IconLink|Relentless}}. However, this requires that all units have at least {{Health|14}} to survive a single attack, or some way of applying defensive buffs; this will also leave your backliners exposed to the enemy waves in between attacks.

If you have access to cheap units like [[Rubble Morsel]] and the space to play them, you can simply put them in front of your more important units and let '''Arkion''' push them back, killing them in the process.

== Corrupted Mass ==
In this variant, '''Fleshlings''' have {{AttackHealth|3|3}} and apply {{IconLink|Corruption|1}} to units that kill them. If the Titan Trial is activated, they instead have {{AttackHealth|5|5}} and apply {{IconLink|Corruption|2}} to units that kill them, and '''Fleshweaver''' has {{IconLink|Mass|9}}.
===Strategy===
'''Corrupted Mass''' has the weakest '''Fleshlings''', but applying {{IconLink|Corruption}} to your backline can be quite dangerous for low-{{Health}} attackers. This literally goes double for the Titan Trial - a unit that kills a '''Fleshling''' on turn one will lose at least {{Health|12}} by {{IconLink|Relentless}}. Ways to bolster {{Health}} or keep your units safe, like {{IconLink|Lifesteal}}, {{IconLink|Armor}}, or upgrades like {{IconLink|Heartstone}} and {{IconLink|Largestone}}, are paramount.

Killing '''Fleshlings''' with spells is important in this fight, as they are both relatively easy to kill even with unupgraded spells and have the most punishing effect on your units. Killing them with spells prevents them from applying any {{IconLink|Corruption}} at all. With the Titan Trial activated, '''Fleshlings''' are out of range of spells like [[Torch]] and [[Glimmer]], but will still fall to [[Frozen Lance]] and most drafted spells like [[Antumbra Assault]] and [[Golden Touch]]. Keep in mind that area-of-effect damaging spells will damage all '''Fleshlings''' on the floor, but they will also spawn a new one if they hit '''Fleshweaver''' and he still has {{IconLink|Mass}}. They can also be used to take out [[Misshapen Fiend]]s, but this will unfortunately not prevent them from applying {{IconLink|Corruption}} to your front unit.

== Spiked Mass ==
In this variant, '''Fleshlings''' have {{AttackHealth|2|5}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|1}}. If the Titan Trial is activated, they instead have {{AttackHealth|3|9}} and {{IconLink|Spikes|2}}, and '''Fleshweaver''' has {{IconLink|Mass|9}}.
===Strategy===
Like the above variant, '''Spiked Mass''' pressures your backline units, but generally less so since {{IconLink|Spikes}} will not continue to damage your units throughout the battle. In exchange, however, the '''Fleshlings''' are quite a bit more durable, out of range of a lot of basic spells with the Titan Trial active. At exactly {{Health|9}}, a [[Shield Steward]] cannot kill them in one hit without upgrades. Most banner units can, but certain ones like [[Miser]] and [[Lunar Priestess]] fail to do so. Once again, investing in healing or protective measures is valuable, especially for extremely fragile units like [[Nightingale]] and [[Animus of Speed]].

[[Cowering Sycophant]]s appear in every wave, amplifying the damage from {{IconLink|Spikes}} even if you don't strip {{IconLink|Mass}} from '''Fleshweaver'''. They will deal a minimum of 12 extra damage to the unit that hits first each round across the entire combat, on top of '''Fleshling''' damage. This can make fragile {{IconLink|Quick}} units more risky if you cannot bolster their {{Health}} somehow. Backline access is also very important in this fight, as otherwise [[Lurking Miscreant]]s will clog up your draw pile.

== More Mass ==
In this variant, '''Fleshlings''' have {{AttackHealth|5|5}}. '''Fleshweaver''' also has {{IconLink|Mass|8}} instead of {{IconLink|Mass|5}}. If the Titan Trial is activated, they instead have {{AttackHealth|7|7}}, and '''Fleshweaver''' has {{IconLink|Mass|12}}.
===Strategy===
'''More Mass''' does not threaten your backline directly, but it is far more dangerous for your frontliners, and this is reflected in the waves as well. '''Fleshweaver''' enters with a much higher {{Attack}} and is much more likely to survive to {{IconLink|Relentless}} with extra stacks of {{IconLink|Mass}}. The increased stats on '''Fleshlings''' are not usually too bad if you have ways of replenishing your defenses, but if you are relying on pure bulk and cannot supplement it throughout the battle, they can overrun your frontliners quickly. Notably, if you place a [[Shield Steward]] alone on the top floor, [[Fleshweaver]]'s attack will leave it with only {{Health|2}}, letting the spawned '''Fleshling''' kill it and then ascend to your Pyre.

The biggest danger of the Titan Trial is his tremendous starting {{IconLink|Mass}}. Starting with {{Attack|31}} puts an overwhelming amount of pressure on your frontliners. Upgrades like {{IconLink|Largestone}} and {{IconLink|Titanstone}} are vital for this fight, as there are very few units who can absorb his immense damage output in the first stages of the fight. Even strong tanks like [[Prickly Puffball]], [[Titan Sentry]], and [[Firebrand]] can easily fall within the first three rounds of combat. Furthermore, if he successfully kills your units, that means you are much less likely to actually damage him and thus remove {{IconLink|Mass}} stacks, making for a more difficult {{IconLink|Relentless}} phase.

The boosted stats on '''Fleshlings''' are generally not very dangerous compared to '''Fleshweaver''' himself, but they put even more pressure on your tanks, and if they reach your Pyre, they can deal a fair amount of damage. A Shield Steward with a {{IconLink|Heartstone}} on the top floor can safely take a hit, retaliate, and then survive to kill the '''Fleshling''', but will die when he returns. {{IconLink|Quick}} units can kill them without letting them attack, and can also deplete {{IconLink|Mass}} from '''Fleshweaver''' before he attacks, weakening his damage output slightly.

The waves in this fight feature large numbers of [[Forsaken]], which will take many individual hits to clear out if you don't have any area of effect damage, in addition to pressuring your frontliner even further. Furthermore, they will eventually spawn in front of [[Sloven Knight]]s, whose damage will spike once they have all been cleared away. You can spawn '''Fleshlings''' in front of them after the Forsaken are gone to deactivate {{IconLink|Vanguard}}, but with the Titan Trial enabled this only decreases incoming damage by 1 - the Knight loses {{Attack|8}}, but the '''Fleshling''' has {{Attack|7}}. [[Jackstrips]] is a great help in this variant, as eliminating all Forsaken will still drastically decrease incoming damage overall. {{IconLink|Spikes}} can be risky, as you will both take the damage from Forsaken swarms and the increased damage from the Sloven Knights, since the Forsaken will die as they attack and leave the Knight in front.

The [[Chosen Acolyte]]s at Covenant 10 can be dangerous, as they are difficult to kill and can easily undo progress against Sloven Knights, who can easily end your run if they reach your Pyre due to their high {{Attack}}.

== General Strategy ==
It is important to try to deplete as much {{IconLink|Mass}} from '''Fleshweaver''' before {{IconLink|Relentless}} begins, as every stack that remains will grant him a boost to {{Attack}}. Targeted damage spells are hugely useful in this fight, letting you ping '''Fleshweaver''' to deplete his {{IconLink|Mass}}, and eliminate the spawned '''Fleshlings''' without triggering their harmful effects on units. {{IconLink|Sweep}} units can simultaneously kill '''Fleshlings''' and remove {{IconLink|Mass}} stacks if '''Fleshweaver''' is on the floor, but this can be quite dangerous against '''Spiked Mass''' and '''Corrupted Mass''' as it will stack a lot of damage on that unit.

Damage over time effects can also be very strong, as they will cause the boss to lose a stack of {{IconLink|Mass}} every turn. Playing [[Forgone Power]] on '''Fleshweaver''' on the first turn is an easy way to start draining his {{Attack}} immediately. This can make it difficult to deal with the number of '''Fleshlings''' on your train, but also makes '''Fleshweaver''' himself much less dangerous by the time he enters {{IconLink|Relentless}}. [[Penitent's Bloodsuit]] can also achieve the same effect, dealing damage every time it moves, with the extra bonus of doing a hefty chunk of damage.

If you can fully deplete {{IconLink|Mass}} and prevent the '''Fleshlings''' from weakening your units too much, '''Fleshweaver''' is fairly harmless during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, having less {{Attack}} than bosses like [[Elebor the Wall]] and [[Yorael the First-Blessed]], and almost always far less damage than [[Arkion]].

The Titan Trial for all '''Fleshweaver''' variants grants him an additional {{IconLink|Mass|4}}, which gives him enough damage to immediately kill a [[Shield Steward]] without upgrades. This makes him considerably more dangerous, especially combined with the buffed '''Fleshlings'''.

Note that almost all sources of floor-wide damage such as {{IconLink|Sweep}} and spells such as [[Inferno]] deal damage front-to-back, which means that they will hit the regular enemies and any spawned '''Fleshlings''' first, before hitting '''Fleshweaver''' and spawning a new '''Fleshling'''.

== Strategy ==
'''Korin the Judge''' can be an extremely dangerous boss, or a very easy one, depending on your setup going into the battle. When she appears at higher Covenants, she summons all surviving enemy units to the bottom floor and grants them {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}, potentially creating a massive wall of highly damaging units which will tear you apart during the {{IconLink|Relentless}} battle. There are two main ways to deal with this.

Due to the unit limit, '''Korin''' can only summon up to 6 enemies to her floor, and will do so left-to-right, top-to-bottom, so if there are more than 6 enemies present, the back enemies on the second floor will not be summoned to her floor (but will still gain {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}).

The first is to build on the bottom floor, killing units as they enter, so that there are none left for '''Korin''' to summon once she appears. This can be difficult if you are unable to deal with early waves without a turn or two to set up, however, especially with the [[Trials#Mark of Invasion|Mark of Invasion]] trial.

If you cannot afford to build bottom floor, then plan to take out '''Korin''''s allies. The easiest method is to use an [[Ascend]] spell such as [[Hidden Passage]] or [[Rising Rage]], preferably with [[Holdover]] or [[Permafrost]] upgrades to guarantee having it in your hand at the required time. Casting this on the boss will move her up, at which point she will corrupt the floor below and kill everyone else, saving you the trouble of destroying her allies. Alternatively, you can eliminate them with high damage spells, either before she appears or while she ascends. Full-floor damage spells like [[Inferno]] or [[Heavenfall]] are best for this purpose.

If neither of these are an option, then plan to either put up an extremely strong fight on the top floor or die to a wave of powered-up enemies.

In general, '''Korin''' is least threatening in the [[Celestial Forge#Hordes of Heaven|Hordes of Heaven]] battle, as the [[Malevolent Hunter]]s will move ahead of the rest of the wave, and go directly to the 3rd floor due to their {{IconLink|Haste}}, leaving '''Korin''' with only [[Fallen Executioner]]s and [[Misshapen Fiend]]s.

[[Celestial Forge#Savagery's Hunters|Savagery's Hunters]] on the other hand is an extremely dangerous combat for '''Korin''', as she summons [[Ravenous Zealot]]s to the bottom floor with {{IconLink|Multistrike|+1}}, giving them {{IconLink|Multistrike|2}} along with high damage backliners also with {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}}, making for an extremely deadly wave.

== Strategy ==
'''Ajax''''s {{IconLink|Sap}} is not a big deal if you have high-{{Attack}} units, but can be problematic if you're relying on a tanky, lower-{{Attack}} floor to win the {{IconLink|Relentless}} phase. After only a few rounds of combat, your units will be reduced to {{Attack|0}}, and then '''Ajax''' can take as long as he wants to slice through your units. Don't allow yourself to become overly reliant on {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, which increases the effect of {{IconLink|Sap}} on your units, and focus on getting big {{Attack}} numbers before he arrives. Preferably {{Attack|>100}} or {{Attack|70x2}} or {{Attack|60x3}} on [[Covenant Rank]] 8 or higher; for details see the math section below.

'''Ajax''''s abilities are completely ineffective against non-{{Attack}} damage sources like {{IconLink|Spikes}}, {{IconLink|Decay}}, {{IconLink|Frostbite}} or {{IconLink|Unstable}}. With a strong enough defense, any damage-over-time effect can take him down relatively easily, as his damage output is very low for this point in the game. Alternatively, any sources of mid-combat damage scaling like [[Everlasting Light]] or [[Lava Armor]] will make the fight much easier by countering his {{IconLink|Sap}}. [[Equalizing Rings]] and [[Iron-tongue]] override a unit's {{Attack}} value, and therefore make their holders immune to the effects of {{IconLink|Sap}}.

=== The Math ===
'''Ajax''' inflicts {{IconLink|Sap|3}} per turn on all units and (on [[Covenant Rank]] 4+) another {{IconLink|Sap|3}} on the frontline unit. {{IconLink|Sap}} decays by 1 per turn, so on turns 1, 2, 3 your surviving backline units have {{IconLink|Sap|3}}, {{IconLink|Sap|5}}, {{IconLink|Sap|7}}, etc. and your frontline unit has {{IconLink|Sap|6}}, {{IconLink|Sap|11}}, {{IconLink|Sap|16}}, etc. (The numbers become a bit more unpredictable once the initial frontline unit dies.)

Suppose a unit has {{Attack|A}} and N strikes per turn, and it survives for T turns before '''Ajax''' reduces it to {{Attack|0}} on turn T+1. How much damage does this unit inflict on '''Ajax''' in total?

Answer:

Final turn with damage: '''T = ⌊(A - 3) / 4⌋''' (brackets = floor function = round down)

If T>0, then the unit inflicts a total damage D of: '''D = N × T × (A - 4 - 2T)'''

For A>20, this formula can be approximated well as '''D ≈ A² / 8 - A'''

==== Example ====

Unit with A = 20 and N = 2:

T = ⌊(20-3)/4⌋ = ⌊17/4⌋ = 4

D = 2 × 4 × (20 - 4 - 2×4) = 2 × 4 × 8 = 64

As you can see, even a unit with {{Attack|20}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} only inflicts negligible damage relative to '''Ajax''''s {{Health}}.

Weak, low-{{Capacity}} units like [[Imps]] are often worth playing at the back, where they can be protected and speed up the stripping away of {{IconLink|Reanimate}} stacks. {{IconLink|Spikes}} on your frontliner will do the same.

At higher Covenants, it is usually best to set up on lower floors to prevent '''The Undying One''' from gaining more {{IconLink|Reanimate}} as they ascend. '''Stryx''' is a [[Flying Bosses|major boss]] of [[Ring 6]]. She appears as one of three variants, always together with [[Hallow]]. Unlike most major bosses, she does not fly and instead moves around the train cycling back to the first floor due to having the status effect {{IconLink|Live to Fight|png=LiveToFight}}.

== Bloody Harvest ==
In this variant, '''Stryx''' applies {{Attack|+1}} to Hallow on {{IconLink|Revenge}}. If the Titan Trial is activated, she applies {{Attack|+2}} instead.
===Strategy===
Be wary of using strategies that involve multiple instances of damage, such as {{IconLink|Spikes}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike}}. Each extra hit on '''Stryx''' is a buff to Hallow's {{Attack}}, and if you're not careful you could end up staring down a Hallow with {{Attack|50+}} and {{IconLink|Multistrike|1}} (especially if you enable the Titan Trial) by {{IconLink|Relentless}}. Passive damage effects, like {{IconLink|Decay}} or [[Jackstrips]], can be inadvisable, as they grant her extra {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers. It may also be wise to avoid {{IconLink|Pyregel}} strategies, which tend to rely on amplifying the output of a high number of weak hits. Focus instead on having really high damage output per hit through cards like [[Last Stand]], [[Attuned]] spells with {{IconLink|Conduit}}, or sources of {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} or {{IconLink|Spell Weakness}}, so that you can eliminate her in as few hits as possible.

If you have [[Ascend]] or [[Descend]] cards, putting one on '''[[Holdover]]''' is one of the best methods of dealing with her, keeping her trapped on an empty floor each turn and preventing her from triggering {{IconLink|Revenge}}; {{IconLink|Rooted}} can achieve the same thing, although you'll eventually need to fight her in {{IconLink|Relentless}} anyways, and she retains her {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger, so you cannot avoid buffing Hallow entirely.

Playing on the top floor is highly advisable if you do not have any way to shut her down. She will only appear on the top floor twice, compared to thrice on the bottom floor, meaning she will get fewer {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers. Additionally, unlike in other variants, the only units that spawn behind her are [[Malevolent Hunter]]s and [[Disciple of Ruin|Disciples of Ruin]]; the Hunters will leave her protection after a turn due to their {{IconLink|Haste}}, while Disciples of Ruin are just healers and cannot directly threaten your Pyre. This makes backline clearing much less important than in the other variants, where [[Vicious Axethrower]]s and [[Sharp-Eye Sniper]]s will reach your Pyre without backline access.

== Doombringers ==
In this variant, '''Stryx''' applies {{Attack|+3}} to Hallow on {{IconLink|Slay}}. If the Titan Trial is activated, she applies {{Attack|+5}} instead.
===Strategy===
In general, this variant is the least threatening out of all three Stryx & Hallow variants:
*While Bloody Harvest's {{IconLink|Revenge}} trigger and Inevitability's {{IconLink|Loop}} trigger are nearly impossible to stop entirely without very specific solutions, this is the only variant where you can shut down Hallow's {{Attack}} gain entirely with a decent deck - a usual strategy of a frontline tank protecting backlines works perfectly fine here.
*The {{Attack}} gain is very low on the hardest trigger of the three variants, for reference:
**Bloody Harvest matches (with the Titan Trial, outpaces) a single {{IconLink|Slay}}'s {{Attack}} gain in three {{IconLink|Revenge}} triggers
**Stryx needs three {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers to outpace a single Inevitibility {{IconLink|Loop}} trigger
 
Avoid dumping unwanted units to clear your deck for this variant, as '''Stryx''' will easily mulch them and turn them into {{Attack}} for her brother; they'll be more of a liability on-field than in your deck, unless you can guarantee she does not get the credit for killing them, such as putting them on a floor where other enemy units will kill them first. [[Inferno Room]] can be a great solution if you're already utilizing it for backline clearing, simply put unwanted units there and let them get roasted.

Stacking {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} on a frontline tank can be very effective, denying '''Stryx''' {{IconLink|Slay}} triggers and also making the {{Attack}} boost to Hallow irrelevant as long as you can stack up enough shields to last through {{IconLink|Relentless}}. A {{IconLink|Reanimate}} tank can be risky to use in this fight, as '''Stryx''' will constantly trigger {{IconLink|Slay}} each time she removes a stack. However, as long as you can stack up sufficient {{IconLink|Reanimate}}, Hallow's extra damage is irrelevant - just be aware that once you run out he will easily tear through all of your units.

Even if '''Stryx''' does not directly get a kill, the [[Sharp-Eye Sniper]]s that spawn behind her can potentially take advantage of a heavily weakened tank in order to trigger their own {{IconLink|Slay}} effect and gain {{IconLink|Rage}}. She will also tank for them and let them reach the Pyre if you have no way of killing backline units. It's advisable to have a targeted spell or a source of backline damage that deals at least 8 damage to kill them, as in wave 4 they will spawn alongside a [[Harpist Protector]] who will grant {{IconLink|Titanskin|5}}.

== Inevitability ==
In this variant, '''Stryx''' applies {{Attack|+8}} to Hallow on {{IconLink|Loop}}. If the Titan Trial is activated, she applies {{Attack|+12}} instead.
===Strategy===
Killing the [[Energizing Flautist]]s is important in every wave. Not only does this give her fewer {{IconLink|Loop}} triggers, but the design of the waves is such that if '''Stryx''' receives {{IconLink|Haste}}, she will end up in front of very high-{{Health}} enemies and tank for them, potentially letting them reach your Pyre without a scratch. This is especially evident in wave 3, where at Covenant 10, if you do not kill the Energizing Flautist in the first wave, she will end up in front of a [[Scarred Sentinel]] and a [[Chosen Sniper]], which have far too much {{Health}} to meaningfully harm with most spells and can do significant damage to your Pyre. Also, note that the [[Sigiled Seaweed]] artifact, while tremendously useful, is not sufficient to handle Energizing Flautists; the {{IconLink|Mute|1}} will run out before enemies move, and they will regain their {{IconLink|Enchant}} effect.

Similarly to Bloody Harvest, a '''[[Holdover]]''' [[Descend]] card can trap her from ever getting to trigger her {{IconLink|Loop}} as long as the Energizing Flautists are eliminated.

If you can eliminate the Flautists consistently, '''Stryx''' will trigger {{IconLink|Loop}} three times total - twice over the natural course of the fight and once when she descends for {{IconLink|Relentless}}. This means you know exactly how much {{Attack}} Hallow will have by the end of the fight ({{Attack|38}} without the Titan Trial, {{Attack|50}} with) and can prepare appropriately. If you are able to [[Descend]] her even once throughout the fight, she will lose a {{IconLink|Loop}} trigger, as she will already be on the bottom floor upon entering {{IconLink|Relentless}}.

== General Strategy ==
'''Stryx''' tends to be significantly less threatening than Hallow during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, as her {{Attack|16x2}}, while certainly hard to stomach, will often pale in comparison to Hallow's {{Attack}} by the end of the fight. Conversely, she is a much bigger threat during the rest of the fight, as she hits very hard right out of the gate, and her triggers are much more dangerous than Hallow's. The defensive scaling necessary to survive a buffed Hallow for several rounds is generally far more difficult to achieve than the offensive scaling required to slay a buffed '''Stryx''' through her extra {{Health}}.

Because '''Stryx''' will block you from damaging the units behind her, {{IconLink|Sweep}} is very effective at taking out other units, especially because the waves that she tanks for are only made out of fragile backliners. Even if most of your damage is coming from a non-{{IconLink|Sweep}} unit, having someone who can take out these enemies is very useful. Alternatively, full-floor damage spells like [[Glimmer]] or a lot of single-target spells like [[Torch]] can take care of the backliners, but this can be inconsistent.

Using [[Descend]] cards ideally with {{IconLink|Keepstone}}, along with at least one empty floor can entirely neutralize the danger she poses for every variant. By keeping her on an empty floor, she cannot trigger {{IconLink|Revenge}}, {{IconLink|Slay}}, or {{IconLink|Loop}}, and unlike [[Savagery]] or '''Pyre Hunter''' [[Arkion]], she has no means of directly punishing the player for such a move. However, the relative rarity of Descend cards means this may not be an option for your clan combination. [[Ascend]] cards also work for any variant other than '''Inevitability''', though be aware that this forces you to only play a single floor. As she is not immune to {{IconLink|Rooted}} until she enters {{IconLink|Relentless}}, it's also a viable alternative to [[Descend]].

{{IconLink|Mute}} is another way to solve the problem she poses, disabling all of her triggers. [[Chicot]] is an excellent artifact into any version of this boss fight. If you have a limited supply of {{IconLink|Mute}} and cannot keep it applied to both her and her brother, prioritize her, since as stated before she generally has the more dangerous triggers. {{IconLink|Mute}} will also prevent her from granting {{IconLink|Multistrike}} to Hallow on {{IconLink|Extinguish}} and stop {{IconLink|Relentless}} from immediately initiating.

To deal with her high damage output, consider using {{IconLink|Sap}}, {{IconLink|Dazed}}, or strong tanks with {{IconLink|Titanite}} or {{IconLink|Titanskin}}. Chump blockers are generally less effective due to her {{IconLink|Multistrike}} and her {{IconLink|Slay}} trigger in the '''Doombringers''' variant.

If you are playing [[Melting Remnant]], a niche way to stop her triggers is to use [[Intent on Death]] on Hallow (not her - you don't want to give Hallow free {{IconLink|Multistrike}}!) to trigger his {{IconLink|Extinguish}} which will start {{IconLink|Relentless}} early, causing them to lose their triggers. While this gives up many turns for your own units to scale, it can be worth it occasionally if you have a really bad matchup against her, and will likely buff Hallow to insane amounts of {{Attack}}.

==Notes==
* Her abilities will trigger on [[Hallow]] even if he is not on the same floor.
* She is the older sister of [[Hallow]].
* She uses [[Entropy]]'s art when corrupting a floor, despite being blessed by [[Savagery]]; this is likely to match with [[Hallow]] who is blessed by [[Entropy]].
* Killing Stryx will not trigger {{IconLink|Celebrate}} despite it stating that it triggers when a boss is killed, as it actually triggers when a battle ends.

'''Rax the Overblessed''' is one of the possible [[Ring 7]] Bosses. He deals very high damage, strikes twice, and gets even stronger if allowed to {{IconLink|Resolve}}.

== Strategy ==
Many bosses in Monster Train 2 become stronger as they move up the train, in order to disincentivize always playing units on the top floor. '''Rax''' takes this to its logical extreme, becoming absurdly strong with each empty floor he passes through. At Covenant 10, his damage ranges from {{Attack|30x2}} to {{Attack|58x4}} depending on whether he is on the bottom or top floor. Allowing him to {{IconLink|Resolve}}, especially at higher Covenants where he gains {{IconLink|Multistrike}}, can spell the end of an otherwise strong run.

The simplest solution to this fight is to simply play your main units on the bottom floor. This may cause trouble earlier in the battle, but is almost always the right choice, making the fight against '''Rax''' himself far more manageable. Any source of {{IconLink|Mute}} or {{IconLink|Dazed}} can also limit his ability to buff himself even while playing on the upper floors. Alternatively, you can [[Ascend]] him up to the top floor if you wish to set up there and have those cards available.

If you absolutely must play top floor and have no method to stop his buffs, then you will need to build a defense so effective that it can kill an enemy with {{Health|2125}} and {{IconLink|Regen|58}} which deals ~232 damage per turn. Even the toughest units will quickly fall to this amount of damage, and so your only real hope is to deal such enormous damage each turn that he dies before he can tear his way through all of your units. {{IconLink|Dazed}} is effective against him, buying a few extra turns to kill him before his damage can overcome you. A {{IconLink|Steelguard}} unit can also work, though even then he will be dealing 60 damage every round, so you must have a lot of {{IconLink|Armor}}.

[[Cleansing Water]] and [[Resin Removal]] can remove his buffs, making him significantly easier to overcome, especially on the bottom floor. However, Cleansing Water will not prevent him from gaining buffs on {{IconLink|Resolve}} and only has a 50% chance to trigger, while on higher Covenants, Resin Removal will not remove his {{IconLink|Multistrike}}.

He applies {{IconLink|Corruption|2}} to your units on {{IconLink|Action}} and doubles {{IconLink|Corruption}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}. If the [[Trials#Boss_Variants|Titan Trial]] is activated, his {{IconLink|Action}} instead applies {{IconLink|Corruption|4}}.

During the {{IconLink|Relentless}} phase, his {{IconLink|Action}} trigger is disabled, but his {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger remains active.

== Strategy ==
The fight against the Dominant variant of Seraph can be summed up in one word: {{IconLink|Corruption}}. His waves are full of [[Misshapen Fiend]], [[Blightbound Guardian]], and [[Deformed Duo]]. But the main threat is Seraph himself. He applies {{IconLink|Corruption}} to your entire floor, which will quickly kill any units without survivability. He also doubles the front unit's {{IconLink|Corruption}} on {{IconLink|Strike}}. {{IconLink|Mute}} and {{IconLink|Dazed}} will shut down Seraph's abilities, and enough {{IconLink|Sap}} will prevent the {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger, but many decks will lack reliable access to these debuffs. If you can '''[[Ascend]]''' or '''[[Descend]]''' him off of your main floor consistently, this will also keep your important units alive.

Seraph's {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger may not do much to a frontline tank at first, but exponential growth will catch up to even the tankiest unit. High {{Health}} and {{IconLink|Regen}} become useless, and at some point only {{IconLink|Reanimate}} and {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} can keep your frontline alive.  Alternatively, {{IconLink|Endless}} units and throwaway units like [[Morsels]] or [[Funguy]] can prevent Seraph from striking your units as long as the waves are dealt with.

Speaking of which, the waves are mercifully far less threatening than the waves of the other two Seraph variants. Besides the {{IconLink|Corruption}} units and [[Avowed Gladiator|Avowed Gladiators]], the main threats are the scourge-shuffling [[Discordant Heretic]] and (at Covenant 10) [[Chosen Supplicant]]. Be sure to prepare a solution for killing these enemies on the bottom floor if possible.

It is a lot more important in this fight to have effects like {{IconLink|Sweep}}, {{IconLink|Trample}}, or just a really high number of individual attacks than against the other variants of Seraph. Almost every wave will have a Misshapen Fiend or two at the front of the floor to absorb the first few attacks from your units, and later waves will have two Deformed Duos in front of a Heretic or Supplicant, requiring six (!) hits to kill both of them and one more to hit the unit they're protecting. And of course, that's ''after'' you kill the Blightbound Guardians and [[Avowed Gladiator]]s in front of them.

[[Inferno Room]] is incredibly useful here, and it may be worth picking up even if you have no use for it earlier. It kills all [[Scourge]] enemies before they can act, making it safe to build your main defenses on any floor. It will also prevent Misshapen Fiend from applying {{IconLink|Corruption}} to your units (which, due to Seraph's ability to double {{IconLink|Corruption}}, is much more of a downside than usual). [[Zone of Silence]] will also prevent all {{IconLink|Corruption}} application on the floor from anything except Seraph himself. {{IconLink|Steelguard}} either through [[Machinist's Tome]] or [[Steel Steward]] is an incredible hard counter to Seraph's scaling {{IconLink|Corruption}} - even {{IconLink|Corruption|9999}} will get capped to 15 damage

Because Seraph retains his {{IconLink|Strike}} trigger during {{IconLink|Relentless}}, this phase is often a damage race. The fewer rounds of combat it takes to kill him, the better. == Strategy ==
In some ways, the the '''Entropic''' variant of '''Seraph''' is easier to prepare for than the other two variants. This is because:
* Neither '''Seraph''' nor his waves have access to your backlines, allowing you to focus survivability on your frontline tanks.
* There are no enemies that punish top-floor play besides [[Scarred Sentinel]], and no particular urgency to clear enemies on the bottom floor most of the time.
* The [[Curse of Entropy]] on {{IconLink|Resolve}} is identical to [[Entropy]] - if you're preparing to fight the Titans then this should be something you've prepared for anyways.

Nevertheless, the combat does pose unique challenges:
* Unless you have access to {{IconLink|Mute}} or {{IconLink|Dazed}}, your draw will inevitably be polluted with [[Curse of Entropy]]. Each time you draw it, you must decide whether to take Pyre damage, or play it and accept the {{IconLink|Sap}} (on top of the {{IconLink|Sap}} already applied by '''Seraph'''). If your units are relatively weak, it's usually a good idea to simply accept the Pyre damage to ensure that you can kill the relatively tanky waves.
** [[:Category:Discard cards|Discard]] effects, found with the [[Stygian Guard]], are very useful here. Since Curse of Entropy is '''[[Ephemeral]]''', discarding it with a card like [[Offering Token]] or [[Frenzied Swarm]] eliminates it without harming your Pyre or applying {{IconLink|Sap}}.
* Given all of the {{IconLink|Sap}}, you might think that damage spells are an ideal strategy for waveclear. Unfortunately, all waves have [[Purified Soul|Purified Souls]] with {{IconLink|Spell Shield|2}}, and nearly every single wave has an [[Enthralled Ardent]] or (at Covenant 10) a [[Chosen Ardent]]. If you don't carefully consider where and when you play spell cards, you'll end up providing massive {{Attack}} increases to the entire train.
** Certain spells still have utility, however. [[Inferno]] is extremely notable; the combination of '''[[Piercing]]''' and its extremely high damage output means it will single-handedly destroy almost every enemy in this fight except for [[Avowed Gladiator]]s and Scarred Sentinels, and the latter will have very little {{Health}} left over. Specifically, it is one of the only spells in the game capable of killing Chosen Ardents in one hit, preventing {{IconLink|Incant}} from triggering.
* [[Deafening Herald|Deafening Heralds]] are also present, which can completely shut down many units if you aren't able to kill them.
* '''Seraph''' himself has more {{Attack}} and {{Health}} than any other variant, so usually requires a very strong floor to take down in {{IconLink|Relentless}}. This will inevitably be hampered by the huge amount of {{IconLink|Sap}} your units will have accumulated.

[[Zone of Silence]] is an extremely useful room, as it will disable both Enthralled Ardents and Deafening Heralds on its floor. Less importantly, it will turn off the {{IconLink|Enchant}} effect of [[Chosen Bastion]]s and the {{IconLink|Resolve}} effect of Scarred Sentinels.

Support units with {{IconLink|Strike}} triggers, like [[Magma Mauler]] and [[Railbeater]], are in particular danger against this variant. {{IconLink|Sap}} can bring them to {{Attack|0}} fairly easily, which will result in them not attacking at all. If you cannot scale {{Attack}} by other means, consider investing in equipment that locks {{Attack}} to a specific value, like [[Iron-tongue]] or [[Equalizing Rings]].

== Strategy ==
The fight against the Savage variant of Seraph contains many threats:
* {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} is a very significant debuff for your units.
** If unable to clear the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} beforehand, the first hit from Seraph will deal 60 damage (90 damage with the Titan Trial) to your front unit, which most units cannot survive. A survival tool with {{IconLink|Seekstone}} is very helpful.
** If possible, get a lower-damage enemy like an [[Avowed Gladiator]] to clear the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} instead of Seraph.
** Buffs such as {{IconLink|Reanimate}} and {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} can also help keep your units alive, though note that taking damage with {{IconLink|Damage Shield}} does not clear {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}}.
** Units with {{IconLink|Endless}} such as [[Prickly Puffball]] will struggle to function since they receive the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} every time they are summoned, leading them to die to the waves very quickly.
** Saving at least {{Ember|1}} during Deployment in order to place a [[Shield Steward]] or other cheap unit on the top floor, then building your main defense on a lower floor, can distract Seraph for a turn and give you a chance to build up your defenses before he attacks your important units.
* Seraph's waves contain dangerous [[Ragewing Assassin|Ragewing Assassins]] that can decimate your backlines. When combined with Seraph's {{IconLink|Rage}} and the {{IconLink|Melee Weakness}} on your units, squishy backline units will not survive long. At Covenant 10, [[Chosen Assassin|Chosen Assassins]], including in the first wave, make survival even more perilous. Kill them with spells or  {{IconLink|Quick}} units before they can attack.
* Seraph's waves are also the tankiest in the entire game, with an Avowed Gladiator in the first wave and multiple tanks in every wave thereafter at Covenant 10. Most decks without [[Luna Coven]] or [[Stygian Guard]] will be reliant on their units to deal massive damage, wave after wave.
* Lastly, [[Terrifying Amalgam|Terrifying Amalgams]] are present in this combat, directly attacking your Pyre if you can't disable them or keep units alive on lower floors. Many decks will be forced to take some Pyre damage from the Amalgams in this combat, so try to prioritize Pyre health and [[Pyre Remains]] prior to the fight.
If you can manage all of these threats, the good news is that, compared to the other variants, this variant is relatively weak in {{IconLink|Relentless}} once you kill his accompanying wave. With a flat {{Attack|30}}, moderate {{Health}}, and no special abilities, most decks making it this far will not struggle to kill Seraph. It's getting there that is the challenge.

The '''Collector''' is a special enemy that always appears in [[Rings]] 1, 2, 4, 5, and 7. At the start of turn 2 or turn 3 of combat, he spawns at the back of a random enemy floor. Killing him grants between 50 and 100 {{Gold}} depending on the Ring. Otherwise, he disappears from combat at the end of the turn. He can also be {{IconLink|Rooted}} or {{IconLink|Dazed}} to prevent him from fleeing. If {{IconLink|Dazed}}, he will not ascend and will instead end up in the front of the floor.

== Strategy ==
While it's not always possible, killing every '''Collector''' is highly desirable, and usually worth sacrificing Pyre health to obtain. In the early game especially, the extra {{Gold|50}} makes it much easier to afford vital early [[Upgrades]] at [[Merchants]].

It is possible to obtain a '''Collector''''s {{Gold}} multiple times using [[Intent on Death]] or {{IconLink|Reanimate}}.

If affected by {{IconLink|Mute}} or {{IconLink|Silence}}, the '''Collector''' will ''not'' drop {{Gold}}, making those effects counterproductive.

== Starter cards capable of killing the Collector ==
The following [[Starter Cards|Starter cards]] can kill the '''Collector''' or otherwise meaningfully interact with it:
* Banished: [[Just Cause]] can '''[[Advance]]''' the '''Collector''' in front of any enemy units.
* Pyreborne: [[Firestarter]] can kill '''Collectors''' in rings 1-2. So can [[Bloated Whelp]], provided that you either have spare {{Capacity}} on the floor or that it's already in play.
* Luna Coven: [[Witchweave]] can kill '''Collectors''' in rings 1-2.
* Underlegion: [[Sporetouch]] can kill '''Collectors''' in all rings.
* Lazarus League: [[Secret Ingredient]] can kill '''Collectors''' in all rings via {{IconLink|Unstable}} from Blast Infusion, or apply {{IconLink|Rooted}} via Enfeebling Infusion, or apply {{IconLink|Reanimate}} via Madman Infusion.
* Hellhorned: [[Torch]] can kill '''Collectors''' until ring 5.
* Awoken: ---
* Stygian Guard: ---
* Umbra: [[Plink]] can kill '''Collectors''' in rings 1-2, if the spell happens to hit the right target.
* Melting Remnant: ---
